chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The best of the dishes to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the vinegar and the oil, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the meal of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.الْأَصْبَاغِ: Dishes/Foods (literally colors, referring to varieties of food)

ai.seo_question: What was the favorite food of the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies vinegar (khal) and oil as the most beloved foods to the Prophet, linking them to the sustenance of previous Prophets. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Sunnah of simplicity and the spiritual purity of humble, natural foods, often cited in discussions on dietary etiquette (adab al-ta'am). The designation of these items as 'food of the Prophets' underscores their status as a symbol of asceticism and divine favor in Islamic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The best of the dishes to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was the vinegar, and the oil, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is a meal of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The best of dishes to the Messenger of Allah was vinegar and oil and he would say it was the food of the Prophets ‘Alayhim al-Salam.’”
